title: Exegesis of Proverbs
english: God sends; for His works are pure and upright. If the works of God are pure and upright, and the mind is one of His works, then the mind was created by the Lord upright and pure.

It is better to dwell on an open corner than in houses inhabited through injustice and in a common house. He set the open corner against the house that is inhabited and common. If the inhabited and common house is wickedness, then the open corner is virtue. A corner, therefore, is a practice of contemplation, touching and being illuminated by the sun of justice. And Paul also rightly said of the high priest of the Jews that the wall was inhabited and would be struck by God. And the Savior in the Gospels said of the Pharisees that they were tombs inhabited. It is also well said of the corner, where the stone lies, rejected by the builders and having become the head of a corner. And he who is not of the one God said 'common'.

A secret gift subdues passions; but he who restrains his temper stirs up a strong gift. A secret gift is such that the left hand does not know what the right hand does. A man wandering from the way of righteousness will find rest in a gathering of giants. The gathering of giants is wickedness and ignorance.

It is better to dwell in a desert land than with a contentious, talkative, and angry woman. And David says: 'In a desert land and uncultivated and without water, thus I appeared to you in the holy [place].' A desert, therefore, is the virtue which does not have the old men dwelling in it, those who decay according to the desires of disease. Therefore the devil does not even find rest in it, if 'he passes through waterless places seeking rest and does not find it'; 'for he himself is king of all those in the waters'; and again of wisdom: 'the dwellings of her are narrow.' If this is so, is not the contentious, talkative, and angry woman wickedness itself?
He makes the one living with her a fighter, a talker, and an angry person.
A desirable treasure rests upon the mouth of the wise; but foolish men swallow it. The wisdom of the Lord rests in the heart of the wise, but foolish men destroy it.

A wise man ascended fortified cities and pulled down the rampart upon which the ungodly had trusted. Wisdom is a fortified city in which the wise dwell, 'demolishing arguments and every exaltation raised up against the knowledge of God' (2 Cor 10:5).

He who guards his mouth and preserves his tongue keeps his soul from distress. Mouth and tongue [are] soul and mind; for soul they say [is] passion and desire, which some call the passive part of the soul.

An ungodly man desires evil desires all day long; but the righteous man shows mercy and compassion without stint. Regarding angels, it is never to desire evil desires; regarding men, it is sometimes to desire and sometimes not to desire evil desires; regarding demons, it is always to desire evil desires. For 'all the day' signifies through life. Such is also 'be in the fear of the Lord all the day,' instead of through life.

A horse is prepared for the day of war; but the help is from the Lord. The mind says 'horse'; for 'will he not mount your horses, and your cavalry is salvation' (Ps 20:7), he says; and regarding Paul, the Lord says, 'to bear my name' (Acts 9:16).

A more excellent name is better than much wealth; but grace is better than silver and gold. He said the virtue signified by the proper name is beautiful; for this beautiful name is that which the signified good possesses. Thus, we shall not praise an unjust woman even if she is called justice, but the one possessing justice, even if she is named injustice.
A rich man and a poor man met one another; but the Lord made both.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
